title: Contact Center Developer
summary: Contact center developers build the phone and chat systems that customer support teams use: IVR menus (the automated 'press 1' prompts), call routing and links to the CRM so agents see who is calling. They work on cloud platforms such as Amazon Connect, NICE CXone or Genesys Cloud, usually in a customer experience or IT services team.
dailyDuties: Build and change IVR and call-routing flows
Write integration functions that look up callers in the CRM
Connect chat, voice and callback channels to agent queues
Test call flows end to end before a release
Fix call drops and flow errors reported by support teams
Meet client teams to turn routing needs into designs

skills.expectation: Build IVR and routing flows on Amazon Connect, NICE CXone Studio or Genesys Cloud Architect
Write integration functions, such as AWS Lambda handlers, behind the call flows
Write integration functions, such as AWS Lambda handlers, behind the call flows
Call CRM and back-office APIs from flows to look up callers and update records
Connect the contact center to a CRM so agents see caller details (CTI)
Test call and chat flows end to end before each release
Turn business call-routing needs into flow designs
Explain designs and issues to client teams, often in US time zones
Use Lambda, DynamoDB, Lex and CloudWatch around Amazon Connect
Store caller and routing data in a key-value store such as DynamoDB
Understand SIP trunks and telephony basics when troubleshooting calls
Monitor queues, flow errors and call quality dashboards
Deploy contact center setup as code
Add AI virtual agents and call summaries to flows
Keep flow exports and integration code in version control
Deliver flow changes in sprints with the client team

certifications.why: Lambda and serverless skills used in Amazon Connect builds
Broader AWS design knowledge for Amazon Connect projects
